boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a dated word-event header, הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.32.1, byte), matching “This is the word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh” (web:Jer.32.1). A ketiv/qere note sits inside the date phrase itself: ketiv בשנת against qere בַּשָּׁנָה֙ (oshb:Jer.32.1, WLC, single-witness). The header closes on a second regnal count, הִ֧יא הַשָּׁנָ֛ה שְׁמֹנֶֽה עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה לִנְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּֽר (oshb:Jer.32.1, byte), matching “which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar” (web:Jer.32.1), naming the king in the resh-family spelling the bytes carry here. A circumstantial notice follows without a break, הָיָ֤ה כָלוּא֙ בַּחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.32.2, byte), matching “Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard” (web:Jer.32.2). A relative clause then names who confined him, אֲשֶׁ֣ר כְּלָא֔וֹ צִדְקִיָּ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר (oshb:Jer.32.3, byte), matching “For Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying,” (web:Jer.32.3), and the charge Zedekiah brings is itself a question quoting, at one remove, Jeremiah’s own earlier announcement against the city: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י נֹתֵ֜ן אֶת הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את (oshb:Jer.32.3, byte), matching “Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will take it;” (web:Jer.32.3), continuing through the king’s own capture, “and Zedekiah king of Judah won’t escape out of the hand of the Chaldeans, but will surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon” (web:Jer.32.4). It closes on Yahweh’s own sentence as Zedekiah’s charge reports it, “though you fight with the Chaldeans, you will not prosper” (web:Jer.32.5). Nothing across these five verses marks a change of speaker away from the narrator’s own third-person report of Jeremiah and Zedekiah; that shift comes only at the next verse, where the account turns to Jeremiah’s own first-person voice, “Jeremiah said,” (web:Jer.32.6), and this row stops short of it.

boundary_rationale: The narration turns to Jeremiah’s own first-person voice, וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ הָיָ֥ה דְּבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.32.6, byte), matching “Jeremiah said,” (web:Jer.32.6) — the command phase of the sign that follows opens at once with a named relative arriving, “Behold, Hanamel the son of Shallum your uncle will come to you, saying,” (web:Jer.32.7), sent to buy “my field that is in Anathoth” (web:Jer.32.7). The performance follows without any further command, וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵ֠לַי חֲנַמְאֵ֨ל בֶּן דֹּדִ֜י כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ אֶל חֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָה֒ (oshb:Jer.32.8, byte), matching “So Hanamel my uncle’s son came to me in the court of the guard according to Yahweh’s word” (web:Jer.32.8) — a WEB paragraph break falls inside this very verse, between the arrival and Jeremiah’s own closing note that he then knew the word was Yahweh’s, a modern formatting fold rather than any textual seam. The purchase itself, the weighing of silver, the sealing and witnessing of the deed, and its delivery to Baruch all continue this same first-person report through וָֽאֲצַוֶּה֙ אֶת בָּר֔וּךְ לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.32.13, byte), matching “I commanded Baruch before them, saying,” (web:Jer.32.13), which opens the interpretation phase: כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.32.14, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says:” (web:Jer.32.14), charging that the deeds be preserved “that they may last many days” (web:Jer.32.14), and closing on the reason given for the whole sign, כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.32.15, byte), matching “For Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says: ‘Houses and fields and vineyards will yet again be bought in this land.’” (web:Jer.32.15). Command, performance, and interpretation are held here as one unit because no addressee shift, frame-owner change, or discourse imperative interrupts them anywhere in between; the seam comes only where Jeremiah turns from reporting the purchase to reporting his own prayer, “I prayed to Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.32.16), and this row is bounded there.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at verse 14, where Yahweh’s own charge to Baruch opens with its own koh-amar formula, was considered; it is rejected because that formula carries no frame-owner change of its own — it is Jeremiah quoting to Baruch what he had already been told — and a symbolic act’s command, performance, and interpretation are held together as one unit absent such a change.

boundary_rationale: A prayer-frame verb opens the unit on its own, וָאֶתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.32.16, byte), matching “I prayed to Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.32.16), turning Jeremiah’s own report from narrating the purchase to addressing God directly. The address opens with a vocative divine title, אֲהָהּ֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Jer.32.17, byte), matching “Ah Lord Yahweh! Behold, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power” (web:Jer.32.17), and states as its own premise “There is nothing too hard for you” (web:Jer.32.17). Praise of Yahweh’s power and justice continues through a recital of the exodus, the gift of the land, and Israel’s own disobedience, unbroken by any new addressee, until a fresh “Behold” turns the address to the present siege, הִנֵּ֣ה הַסֹּלְל֗וֹת בָּ֣אוּ הָעִיר֮ (oshb:Jer.32.24, byte), matching “Behold, siege ramps have been built against the city to take it” (web:Jer.32.24). It closes on the tension between the command just carried out and the circumstance surrounding it, וְאַתָּ֞ה אָמַ֤רְתָּ אֵלַי֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Jer.32.25, byte), matching “You have said to me, Lord Yahweh, ‘Buy the field for money, and call witnesses;’” (web:Jer.32.25), “whereas the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans” (web:Jer.32.25). This whole address to God is held as one unit because it is never interrupted by a new addressee or a change of speaker — it moves from praise through historical recital to present crisis and an unresolved question without ever leaving Jeremiah’s own voice directed at Yahweh; the next word-event formula reopens address as Yahweh’s own reply, “Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.32.26), and this row ends just short of it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Typing this span as a hymn of praise rather than a lament was considered, since verses 17 through 23 are sustained creation-and-exodus praise close in shape to the doxologies elsewhere in the book; it is held here as a personal address to God running to an unresolved question instead, since the unit does not close on praise but on Jeremiah’s own bewildered complaint at the gap between command and circumstance, the same shape the book’s confessions take even though this address carries none of their persecution content.

boundary_rationale: A fresh word-event formula opens the unit, וַיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.32.26, byte), matching “Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.32.26), turning address from Jeremiah’s own prayer to Yahweh’s own reply. That reply opens on a rhetorical question answering the prayer’s own premise, הִנֵּה֙ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֱלֹהֵ֖י כָּל בָּשָׂ֑ר הֲֽמִמֶּ֔נִּי יִפָּלֵ֖א כָּל דָּבָֽר (oshb:Jer.32.27, byte), matching “Behold, I am Yahweh, the God of all flesh. Is there anything too hard for me?” (web:Jer.32.27), and a judgment sentence follows at once, לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.32.28, byte), matching “Therefore Yahweh says: Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon” (web:Jer.32.28), naming the king in the same resh-family spelling read at the chapter’s own opening. The whole indictment is held as one continuous reply because nothing inside it reopens address to a new party; the turn comes only at a compound turn phrase, וְעַתָּ֕ה לָכֵ֛ן (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte), matching “Now therefore” (web:Jer.32.36), that reopens the reply toward this city’s own restoration, and this row stops just short of that turn.

boundary_rationale: A compound turn particle reopens address toward the city itself, וְעַתָּ֕ה לָכֵ֛ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֶל הָעִ֨יר הַזֹּ֜את אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte), matching “Now therefore Yahweh, the God of Israel, says concerning this city, about which you say,” (web:Jer.32.36), quoting back the current public verdict, “It is given into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence” (web:Jer.32.36). The promise that answers it follows without a break, “Behold, I will gather them out of all the countries where I have driven them” (web:Jer.32.37), through an everlasting covenant, “I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from following them, to do them good” (web:Jer.32.40), and joy over their own good, “I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land assuredly with my whole heart and with my whole soul” (web:Jer.32.41). A further formula, כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.32.42, byte), matching “For Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.32.42), carries the same reply forward rather than opening a new one, since no addressee or frame-owner change accompanies it; it bridges directly into the same quoted-objection construction read at this row’s own opening, אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.32.43, byte), matching “Fields will be bought in this land, about which you say,” (web:Jer.32.43), before quoting the same desolate-land verdict in different words, closing the whole chapter on the same field-purchase vocabulary that opened it, כִּֽי אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת שְׁבוּתָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.32.44, byte), matching “for I will cause their captivity to be reversed,” (web:Jer.32.44) “says Yahweh” (web:Jer.32.44). Nothing between verse 36 and the chapter’s own close reopens a frame-owner or addressee shift, so the restoration promise and its own field-purchase close are held as one unit; the next chapter opens its own fresh word-event formula a second time, “Moreover Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah the second time,” (web:Jer.33.1), and this row is bounded at the chapter division just before it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at verse 42, where the reply opens with a further messenger formula, or at verse 43, where the field-purchase vocabulary itself returns, was considered; both are rejected on the same ground applied at this row’s own opening — neither carries a frame-owner or addressee change of its own, and the whole span from verse 36 reads as one sustained promise closing the chapter on the sign it began with.

boundary_rationale: A second word-event formula opens the unit, וַיְהִ֧י דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ שֵׁנִ֑ית (oshb:Jer.33.1, byte), matching “Moreover Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah the second time,” (web:Jer.33.1), and immediately discloses the same setting as the field-purchase account before it, וְהוּא֙ עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ עָצ֔וּר בַּחֲצַ֥ר הַמַּטָּרָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.33.1, byte), matching “while he was still locked up in the court of the guard” (web:Jer.33.1). The reply opens on a self-declaration formula naming Yahweh three times over, כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עֹשָׂ֑הּ יְהוָ֗ה יוֹצֵ֥ר אוֹתָ֛הּ לַהֲכִינָ֖הּ יְהוָ֥ה (oshb:Jer.33.2, byte), matching “Yahweh who does it, Yahweh who forms it to establish it—Yahweh is his name, says:” (web:Jer.33.2), and an invitation follows at once, קְרָ֥א אֵלַ֖י וְאֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ (oshb:Jer.33.3, byte), matching “Call to me, and I will answer you” (web:Jer.33.3), promising to “show you great and difficult things, which you don’t know” (web:Jer.33.3). What follows is bound to that promise by its own opening particle rather than standing as a fresh, unrelated oracle: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַל (oshb:Jer.33.4, byte), matching “For Yahweh, the God of Israel, says concerning the houses of this city” (web:Jer.33.4) — the causal “for” ties the promised great and difficult thing directly to the healing announced next. Healing, forgiveness, and renown before the nations follow without any addressee change through the unit’s own close, “This city will be to me for a name of joy, for praise, and for glory, before all the nations of the earth” (web:Jer.33.9). No frame-owner or addressee shift interrupts this span anywhere between the invitation and its own content; the next fresh promise reopens with its own quoted-objection formula, “Yet again there will be heard in this place, about which you say,” (web:Jer.33.10), and this row is bounded just before that turn.
